title: DeviceBridge · Next
summary: Only the new improvements: internet remote access, Mac support, Android/iPhone companions and trusted reconnection. The existing Windows release is tracked separately.

items.title: Define the two modes and supported device roles
items.plan: Keep local device sharing and add internet remote access. Windows and Mac are computer hosts; Android and iPhone are controllers. Show platform restrictions explicitly.
items.acceptance: A written scope covers both modes, all four platforms, and the limits of controlling phones.
items.evidence: Agreed in this conversation: retain local sharing, add remote computer access on all four platforms, and include trusted reconnection. This completes planning scope only; it does not mean the new apps are built.

items.title: Design the shared session protocol
items.plan: Specify version negotiation, device capabilities, input events, screen/audio channels, permissions, disconnect and reconnect messages. Preserve the existing Windows mode.
items.acceptance: A documented protocol and compatibility tests cover new clients and the existing Windows app.

items.title: Create the common app interface
items.plan: Use shared screens for devices, modes, QR/key pairing, remote controls, permissions and session status; add native platform modules underneath.
items.acceptance: The same core flow works on small phone screens and Windows/Mac desktops.

items.title: Define supported versions and hardware
items.plan: Choose minimum Windows, macOS, Android and iOS versions after testing capture, codecs and audio support. Include Apple Silicon and decide Intel Mac coverage.
items.acceptance: Publish a supported-device matrix based on actual builds and test results.

items.title: Build the pairing and presence service
items.plan: Run a small authenticated HTTPS/WebSocket service for pairing, device availability and connection setup. Keep screen/audio content out of service logs.
items.acceptance: Two devices on different networks discover each other without opening router ports.

items.title: Add QR codes and six-character pairing keys
items.plan: Use short-lived random keys, strict attempt limits, and first-time approval on the computer; exchange strong device credentials after approval.
items.acceptance: Expired, guessed, replayed and rejected keys cannot authorize a session.

items.title: Save trusted devices and permission choices
items.plan: Store device keys in OS-protected storage. Separate screen viewing, input, microphone and permission to reconnect; allow revocation on the computer.
items.acceptance: A revoked device cannot reconnect and permissions remain scoped to the approved device.

items.title: Connect devices directly with WebRTC
items.plan: Negotiate encrypted video/audio and data channels; use STUN to attempt a direct connection and authenticate the device identity.
items.acceptance: An authorized session works across separate home and mobile networks.

items.title: Add an encrypted relay fallback
items.plan: Provision TURN with short-lived credentials, usage limits and regional configuration. Verify endpoint identity even when using the relay.
items.acceptance: Restrictive networks fall back to TURN successfully, with no unencrypted media.

items.title: Make remote access visible and stoppable
items.plan: Show who is connected, active permissions and a persistent stop action. Release pressed input states and stop audio when access ends.
items.acceptance: Stopping a session promptly ends control and media, including when a client misbehaves.

items.title: Stream the Windows screen
items.plan: Add native screen capture, hardware encoding where supported, display selection and cursor metadata alongside the existing sharing engine.
items.acceptance: A phone sees the selected display smoothly with correct scaling and orientation.

items.title: Receive phone touch, keyboard and trackpad input
items.plan: Map touch and trackpad gestures to mouse actions; support scrolling, dragging, right-click, Unicode text and Windows shortcuts.
items.acceptance: Typing, selection, drag and shortcuts work without stuck keys or duplicate input.

items.title: Send Windows sound to the phone
items.plan: Capture the chosen output, encode it for WebRTC, and handle changes of headphones/speakers with clear status.
items.acceptance: Computer sound reaches the phone and recovers after output-device changes.

items.title: Use the phone microphone inside Windows apps
items.plan: Route received phone audio into the existing virtual microphone path; add mute, level, device selection and guided driver checks.
items.acceptance: A separate calling app records the phone microphone through the selected virtual input.

items.title: Keep the remote host available in the background
items.plan: Extend tray lifecycle handling for internet sessions and offer opt-in start at sign-in. Show locked/asleep/unavailable status honestly.
items.acceptance: Minimize and X preserve sharing; explicit quit stops it. Startup recovery is tested after user sign-in.

items.group: 04 · Native Mac host and local sharing
items.title: Build guided Mac permission setup
items.plan: Request screen/audio capture, input control and microphone access only when needed. Provide status checks and links to the correct macOS settings.
items.acceptance: Denied or revoked permissions produce useful guidance; no permission is silently bypassed.

items.group: 04 · Native Mac host and local sharing
items.title: Stream the MacBook screen
items.plan: Implement a native ScreenCaptureKit capture and encoding module, display selection, Retina scaling and cursor handling.
items.acceptance: An iPhone and an Android phone can each view the actual Mac desktop on supported macOS versions.

items.group: 04 · Native Mac host and local sharing
items.title: Control the Mac from phone touch and keyboard
items.plan: Use permitted native event APIs after control permission; map Command/Option shortcuts, text, click, drag and scroll.
items.acceptance: Mac apps accept phone text and gestures correctly, including non-English text.

items.group: 04 · Native Mac host and local sharing
items.title: Hear Mac sound on the connected device
items.plan: Capture supported system audio and stream it to the controller, including output changes and interruption handling.
items.acceptance: Mac sound is heard on iPhone, Android and desktop clients.

items.group: 04 · Native Mac host and local sharing
items.title: Prototype and package the Mac virtual microphone
items.plan: Validate an Audio Server Driver Plug-in path, licensing, signing and installation. Route incoming phone microphone audio into the virtual input.
items.acceptance: A separate Mac calling app receives phone audio. Installation and required approvals are documented and tested.

items.group: 04 · Native Mac host and local sharing
items.title: Keep the Mac host running with clear controls
items.plan: Add a menu-bar app, explicit quit/disconnect and opt-in login launch. Report sleep/lock conditions and recover supported sessions.
items.acceptance: Closing the window keeps the host available; quit and shutdown end it safely.

items.group: 04 · Native Mac host and local sharing
items.title: Bring local device sharing to Mac and Windows↔Mac
items.plan: Implement local keyboard/mouse handoff, screen positioning, pointer ownership and supported two-way audio routing. Reuse the secure pairing layer.
items.acceptance: Mac↔Mac and Windows↔Mac pass keyboard, mouse, speaker and microphone acceptance tests.

items.title: Build the Android controller app
items.plan: Implement device list, pairing, remote display, touch/trackpad modes, zoom, orientation and accessible controls.
items.acceptance: A physical Android device controls both a Windows PC and a MacBook.

items.title: Build the iPhone/iPad controller app
items.plan: Implement the same connection and control flow with native Apple permissions, keyboard behavior, audio session management and safe area layouts.
items.acceptance: A physical iPhone controls both a MacBook and a Windows PC.

items.title: Make mobile typing and shortcuts reliable
items.plan: Support phone keyboards, composition/IME, Unicode, editing keys and an extra toolbar for computer-only modifier keys.
items.acceptance: Multilingual text, Backspace, Enter, selection and desktop shortcuts work on both hosts.

items.title: Add phone playback and microphone controls
items.plan: Add clearly labeled sound/microphone controls, native permission handling, mute indicators and interruption recovery.
items.acceptance: Phone microphone reaches the chosen host and host audio plays through the selected phone output.

items.title: Handle phone backgrounding and network changes
items.plan: Follow each mobile OS lifecycle; show paused/disconnected state when suspension prevents a session and reconnect when the app becomes active.
items.acceptance: Calls, app switching, screen locking and Wi-Fi/mobile-data changes do not leave stale control active.

items.title: Add supported phone-screen sharing with honest limits
items.plan: Prototype user-approved broadcasting separately from remote computer control. Do not promise unrestricted iPhone control or system-wide phone microphone replacement.
items.acceptance: Each shipped phone-sharing capability is tested and unsupported actions are clearly identified.

items.title: Show when the computer loses internet
items.plan: Use heartbeats and presence expiry to show PC offline / waiting to reconnect, with last-known status and Reconnect now.
items.acceptance: Disconnect the computer internet while the phone stays online; the phone shows the correct state.

items.title: Reconnect when the computer internet returns
items.plan: Retry with bounded backoff, renew transport and relay credentials, and authenticate the previously approved device. Keep session IDs and stale attempts isolated.
items.acceptance: Restore the computer internet and resume without a fresh key when trusted reconnect was approved.

items.title: Make permission to reconnect explicit
items.plan: Add Allow this trusted device to reconnect during initial approval. Respect revocation, expiry and view/input/microphone choices on every recovery.
items.acceptance: Untrusted or revoked devices need approval; reconnect never broadens the saved permissions.

items.title: Recover from address and connection changes
items.plan: Handle Wi-Fi↔Ethernet and phone Wi-Fi↔mobile data changes through ICE restart or a new authenticated transport.
items.acceptance: Both endpoints recover from address changes without router configuration.

items.title: Clear stuck input and stale media on disconnect
items.plan: Release pressed keys/buttons, restore cursor ownership, reset audio buffers and establish a clean stream on reconnect. Require fresh mic consent if needed.
items.acceptance: Interrupt a session during a drag, key press and microphone use; no stuck state or old audio survives.

items.title: Support opt-in desktop recovery after restart
items.plan: Start the host after sign-in when enabled and advertise availability. Keep pre-sign-in access and waking an offline PC outside the initial promise.
items.acceptance: After restart and sign-in, trusted reconnect works on supported Windows and Mac hosts.

items.title: Provision production hosting and relay operations
items.plan: Choose hosting region and costs, configure HTTPS, short-lived secrets, rate limits, retention and operational checks. No secret keys enter client code or the checklist.
items.acceptance: The production service has documented ownership, costs and tested availability.

items.title: Prepare signed Mac and iOS distribution
items.plan: Build on a Mac, configure Apple developer identities, sign/notarize the Mac installer and distribute the iOS beta through TestFlight before store submission.
items.acceptance: Fresh Mac and iPhone installations succeed through the documented distribution process.

items.title: Package Android and updated Windows releases
items.plan: Create signed Android builds and a versioned Windows installer, preserving the existing working mode and upgrade settings. Signing credentials remain private.
items.acceptance: Install/update/uninstall tests pass; store/release assets match the advertised version.

items.title: Protect the existing Windows local mode
items.plan: Run current regression checks and physical keyboard, mouse, sound, microphone and background-sharing tests after integration.
items.acceptance: The new remote mode does not regress existing Windows-to-Windows functionality.

items.title: Test every main controller-to-computer pairing
items.plan: Test iPhone→Mac, Android→Mac, iPhone→Windows and Android→Windows, plus desktop combinations, using physical hardware on separate networks.
items.acceptance: Record actual results for screen, input, audio, microphone and stop actions for each supported pairing.

items.title: Test internet outages and long sessions
items.plan: Test loss/return of host internet, network switching, revocation, relay-only paths, interruptions and sustained sessions on Windows and Mac.
items.acceptance: Trusted recovery works without repeated approval; unauthorized reconnect is rejected and no stuck input remains.

items.title: Publish the new apps, guides and compatibility matrix
items.plan: Update the website with actual platform downloads, supported features and simple setup steps. Mark features complete only after release evidence is available.
items.acceptance: Public links download the tested signed builds and the checklist reflects actual verified outcomes.
